transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, what scared me enough to actually come in today is... I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. And lately, sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. It frightened me enough to realize I needed to talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about a month. We recently took in a relative, and... well, it's just been this intense up-and-down crisis ever since. That's when these feelings really started getting bad.
Have you ever experienced a period of depression like this before in your life?

Well, to be clear... this current period didn't actually just start a month ago. The depression has actually been hanging over me for about 11 months now. Taking in my relative this past month just made everything feel completely unbearable, but I've been struggling with this same low feeling since way before they moved in.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt unusually energized, wired, or on top of the world, needing much less sleep than normal?

Well, actually... earlier this month, I did have a brief time where I felt almost, I don't know, electrically upbeat. But it didn't stay that way. I just started snapping at everyone over really tiny things. Like, at the clinic, if someone misplaced a medication cup or if there was a sudden change in the morning schedule, I would just lose my temper. It really didn't feel like my usual self at all.
How long did that period of feeling electrically upbeat and irritable last?

I'm not entirely sure exactly how many days it was, to be honest. It just felt like a short stretch earlier this month before I went back to feeling so low. I didn't really track it on a calendar or anything.
Before these past 11 months, had you ever experienced any other separate episodes of depression in your life?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs, but nothing like this. This past year is really the first time I've ever felt this... this bad.
During that stretch when you felt electrically upbeat and irritable, did you find you needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
Yes, actually. During that high-energy stretch, I was sleeping maybe three hours a night. I'd still get up before sunrise feeling sharp, totally convinced I didn't really need more rest.
During that stretch, did you feel like your thoughts were racing or moving much faster than usual?

No, I don't think so. Um, my mind felt pretty clear, actually. I mean, I had all that physical energy, but my thoughts weren't really racing or spinning out of control or anything like that. They just felt normal to me.
During that high-energy stretch, did you find yourself taking on a lot of extra projects or tasks that you wouldn't normally do?

Yes, I did. I actually took on a lot. Um, I picked up extra shifts at work, and then at home, I completely redid our whole household care schedule. I started contacting contractors for things around the house, and... I was trying to coordinate everyone's tasks like it was some major hospital project. No one had even asked me to take that much on, but I just did it all anyway.
During that stretch, did you find yourself talking much more or faster than you normally do?

No, not really. I mean, I was definitely more active and getting a lot done, but I didn't notice myself talking any faster or more than usual. People seemed to understand me just fine, and no one mentioned that I was talking too much. I was just focused on getting things done.
During that high-energy stretch, did you find yourself doing anything unusually impulsive or risky, such as spending excessive money or making uncharacteristic decisions?

Yes, actually. I... I spent a lot of money without really thinking it through. I bought all this stuff for the house—like, monitoring equipment, ramps, special bedding, just a ton of supplies. At the time, it felt like I absolutely had to have it right then, like it was urgently necessary. But looking back... well, I put a lot of charges on our credit card, and we really can't cover them.
